rationale: The assistant went straight to the sensible first step (unplug, turn drum by hand), correctly interpreted the free-spinning drum and visible black strip as a snapped belt, and matched the hidden truth including the idler/jockey pulley advice. It handled the partial model number well, avoided naming an exact part number and instead told the customer to read the code off the old belt. Minor weaknesses: '$10–25' pricing in the first reply for a UK customer, belt-fitting instructions repeated across both replies, no mention of the capacitor/sharp edges, and no engineer fallback offered.
